svg.title: Pi Pico 2 — Sensor Wiring Detail
svg.desc: Every pin of the Pico with wire color, function, and the sensor it connects to.
svg.text: Every used pin colored by function. Wire colors match docs/hardware.md convention.

g.text: Inside the hive · SHT31-DIS-F variant recommended for propolis resistance
In Stevenson-style radiation shield, ~1 m from hive
4.7 kΩ pull-up · top / above brood / brood-side / entrance
Under the hive stand · dedicated bit-banged GPIO
SHIELDED CAT6 required — data pair + power pair, foil to Pico GND only
50 kg half-bridge bar cells (E+/E-/A+/A- wired diagonally)
Everlight ITR9606 slotted opto-interrupters (5 mm gap)
Beam A = outer, Beam B = inner · direction from trip order
Pack up to 12.6 V → ADC sees 2.27 V (safe under 3.3 V max)
• All sensors are 3.3 V native — powered from the Pico's 3V3_OUT (pin 36). Do NOT connect any 5 V-only sensor without a level shifter.
• I²C0 (SHT41 + BME280) and I²C1 (VEML7700 + SCD41 + SGP40) are separated so a hung sensor on one bus doesn't kill the other.
• 4.7 kΩ pull-up on 1-Wire (GP22 → 3V3). I²C pull-ups live on the sensor breakouts.
• HX711 to Pico uses SHIELDED CAT6. Foil drain terminates at the Pico GND end only. Keep run under 1 m.
• Bee-gate phototransistors are pulled up with 10 kΩ to 3V3. IR LED side gets a 220 Ω series resistor from 3V3. All 16 phototransistor emitters return to Pico GND.
• RUN pin (30) is wired to Pi GPIO23 — the Pi can pulse it low to hard-reset the Pico if serial packets stop arriving for > 30 s.
• Conformal-coat every PCB going into or near the hive with MG Chemicals 419D — mask sensor apertures (SHT41 opening, DS18B20 tips, IR slot) before spraying.
